references.comment: In UsernameForm.authenticate(), isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without passing the required UserModel parameter.

With isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user) requiring user != null, authenticate(...) will not call webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context) on the initial login page where context.getUser() is still null, so conditional passkey UI will not be set up for first-time passkey login. Consider whether this should also be enabled when no user has been selected yet so ID-less passkey authentication on the initial login form continues to work.

rows.label: match
rows.reason: Finding 0 and reference 0 both identify the same concrete bug: isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() is called without the required UserModel argument in UsernameForm.java line 47, which would cause a compilation error.

rows.label: false_positive
rows.reason: The action() method in UsernamePasswordForm.java returns early when validateForm() returns false, but this is the standard pattern in Keycloak authenticators — validateForm/validateUserAndPassword internally calls context.failureChallenge() or context.challenge() before returning false, so no additional failure handling is needed.

rows.reason: The test in PasskeysUsernameFormTest.java sets the policy to YES/REQUIRED and then checks for YES/REQUIRED — there is no mismatch. The finding incorrectly claims null values are set; the actual code sets Constants.WEBAUTHN_POLICY_OPTION_YES and Constants.WEBAUTHN_POLICY_OPTION_REQUIRED.

rows.reason: Changing USER_SET_BEFORE_USERNAME_PASSWORD_AUTH from protected to public is intentional here (it is now referenced from AuthenticatorUtils in a different package), making the visibility change necessary. Whether this constitutes an undesirable API exposure is subjective and context-dependent.
